newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Burma's Suu Kyi asks for international support.
newsitem.headline: Burma's Suu Kyi asks for international support.

text.p: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi, saying she had not been allowed to leave her home since Monday's student protests in Rangoon, appealed on Tuesday for moral and practical support for her party.
Speaking by telephone to former Commonwealth secretary general Sonny Ramphal in Cape Town, Suu Kyi said: "I would like the world to know that the repression in Burma is getting worse."
She said she had been prevented by police from leaving her home since student protests erupted there on Monday, resulting in the arrest of 300 demonstrators.

Suu Kyi, a Nobel peace laureate and leader of the National League for Democracy, is a member of the board of Ramphal's Stockholm-based International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (IDEA), which met in Cape Town.

"We as a party are subjected to so much persecution that it is almost unbelievable. We are supposed to be a legitimate party, duly registered, and yet we are not even allowed to do regular party work," she said in a call taped and played to reporters.
"My house is barricaded off every weekend and today it is barricaded off and probably they will close off the street for a few days to come.

"Members of our party are subjected to very, very severe persecution all the time. People are evicted from their homes, people have been threatened with loss of jobs and our elected members of parliament are forced to resign," she said.
"We would welcome the moral and practical support of right thinking people ...," she said.
Ramphal promised to broadcast Suu Kyi's appeal adding "where better to send that message to the world than from South Africa".

He began the conversation by discussing IDEA's efforts to get reports to her, but the two agreed not to discuss the issue on the telephone after she warned that she seldom received mail addressed to her.
"I think it is best that we should not talk about that," she said.
